# @dolphin278/vjuga

> Zero-dependency, ESM-only TypeScript utility library. Node >=22.
> Install: `npm install @dolphin278/vjuga`
> There is no root export. Import a module subpath:
> `import * as LRUCache from "@dolphin278/vjuga/LRUCache"`
> All modules are standalone ESM files — import only what you need.

After install, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) then one file:
`node_modules/@dolphin278/vjuga/src/<Module>.d.ts` (schema modules: `src/schema/`).

## Error Handling

- `@dolphin278/vjuga/Result.js`: `Result<T,E>` — tuple-encoded discriminated union `[boolean, T|E]` for fallible operations. `ok(v)` / `err(e)` constructors (`const` type params, so `ok(true)` is `Ok<true>`); `isOk`, `isErr`, `map`, `mapErr`, `flatMap`, `unwrapOr`, `unwrap`, `fromThrowable`, `fromPromise`, `fromAsyncThrowable` (never throws synchronously; mapper exceptions reject). Return errors as values instead of throwing. For 3+ variants use `TaggedUnion`.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/ErrorChain.js`: `ErrorChain` — traverse ES2022 `Error.cause` chains. `chain(e)` → iterator, `toArray(e)`, `find(predicate, e)`. Cyclic chains terminate. Use when inspecting or searching a wrapped error chain.

## Data Structures

- `@dolphin278/vjuga/Queue.js`: `Queue` — circular-buffer deque with power-of-2 capacity. O(1) `push`, `pop`, `shift`, `unshift`, `peekFront`, `peekBack`, `get`, `set`. Grows and shrinks. Use for FIFO/LIFO queues larger than ~16 items where `Array.shift()` O(n) cost matters.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/PriorityQueue.js`: `PriorityQueue` — binary min-heap. O(log n) `push` and `pop`; O(1) `peek`; O(n) `heapify` for bulk init. Supply a comparator at construction. Not stable; a throwing comparator leaves the heap unchanged. Use for repeated min-element extraction (task scheduling, Dijkstra, timer heaps).
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/LRUCache.js`: `LRUCache` — bounded cache with Least-Recently-Used eviction backed by doubly-linked list + Map. `make(capacity)`, `get`, `set`, `has`, `del`, `size`. For `Memoization`, wrap it as `{ get, has, set }`. Use when you want to cap memory while keeping the hottest items fast.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/WeakCache.js`: `WeakCache` — GC-managed cache via `WeakRef` + `FinalizationRegistry`. `make()`, `get`, `set`, `has`, `remove`, `size`. Entries are reclaimed automatically when values are garbage-collected. Values must be objects.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/RadixTree.js`: `RadixTree` — compressed trie (patricia trie) mapping string keys to values. `insert`, `lookup`, `has`, `remove`, `prefixMatch`, `entries`, `size`. `entries`/`prefixMatch` return lexicographic order; `insert(k, undefined)` removes. Use for URL routing, autocomplete, prefix-based lookups.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/SOA.js`: `SOA` — Structure of Arrays with zero-copy element views. `createView`, `push`, `pop`, `get`, `set`, `getSlice`, `length`, `swapRemove`, `clear`. `set` throws `RangeError` unless `0 <= i < length`; `index` is a reserved column name; the column set must not change after the first `get`/`pop`. Use for cache-line-efficient iteration over many records (physics loops, ECS engines, columnar transforms).
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/BloomFilter.js`: `BloomFilter` — probabilistic membership filter (Bloom filter). `make(capacity, fpr?)`, `add`, `mightContain`, `clear`, `count`, `bitCount`, `hashCount`. Strings only; `make` throws `RangeError` if `fpr` is unreachable or NaN (m capped at 2^32 bits). Never yields false negatives. Use as a fast pre-filter before expensive cache or database lookups.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/BitSet.js`: `BitSet` — compact bit array backed by `Uint32Array`. `make(capacity)`, `set`, `clear`, `toggle`, `get`, `capacity`, `popcount` (SWAR), `toArray`. Set algebra: `and`, `or`, `xor`, `not` (return new BitSet). Use for dense boolean vectors, graph adjacency, SOA row-level flags.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/OrderedMap.js`: `OrderedMap` — sorted key-value map backed by an AVL tree. `make(compare?)`, `set`, `get`, `has`, `del`, `size`, `min`, `max`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `range`, `forRange(m, lo, hi, fn)` (hot path), `keys`, `values`, `entries`. Default comparator is a total order (NaN last, `-0` equals `0`). Use when sorted iteration or floor/ceiling/range queries are needed; for unordered lookup use plain `Map`.

## Async & Concurrency

- `@dolphin278/vjuga/BatchExecutor.js`: `BatchExecutor` — dataloader-style batching with per-item promise results. `make(batchFn, options?)` returns `(item) => Promise<R>`; `options` is a `ScheduleMode` string (`"macrotask"` default, `"io"`) or `{ schedule?, maxBatchSize?, maxInFlight? }`. N concurrent callers get individual results; underlying work is batched. `maxBatchSize` splits a tick's items into chunks; `maxInFlight` caps concurrent `batchFn` invocations, queuing further chunks FIFO across ticks (limits: integer >= 1 or `Infinity`, else `RangeError` from `make`). Batch fn must return exactly as many `PromiseSettledResult` items as received; a length mismatch, throw or rejection rejects every promise in that chunk only. For fire-and-forget batching use `BufferizedFunction`.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/BufferizedFunction.js`: `BufferizedFunction` — fire-and-forget call batching. `make(fn, schedule?)` collects args then calls `fn(batch)` on next tick. Use for logging, analytics, telemetry where callers do not need per-item results. Schedule: `"macrotask"` (default) or `"io"`.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/TimedFunction.js`: `TimedFunction` — `throttle(fn, ms)` leading-edge (fires immediately, drops calls within window including re-entrant ones; a throwing `fn` still starts the window — scroll/resize) and `debounce(fn, ms)` trailing-edge (fires after silence — search input, resize-end).
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/PromiseUtils.js`: `PromiseUtils` — parallel resolution of named promise records plus an async concurrency limiter. `props({ a: pa, b: pb })` → `{ a, b }`; `propsMap(map)` → `Map`. `props` resolves own enumerable string and symbol keys and returns a null-prototype object. Use instead of positional `Promise.all` when named results are clearer. `pool(items, limit, fn, { signal? })` runs `fn(item, index, signal)` over any iterable with at most `limit` calls in flight (integer >= 1 or `Infinity`), starting in input order, and resolves to `PromiseSettledResult[]` in input order (never rejects for `fn` failures; invalid arguments reject). After `signal` aborts no new calls start, unstarted items reject with `signal.reason`, in-flight calls finish. In-process async I/O limiter — use `WorkerPool` for CPU-bound work on threads.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/WorkerPool.js`: `WorkerPool` — thread pool via `node:worker_threads`. `make(config)`, `run(pool, data, opts?)`, `drain(pool)`, `destroy(pool)`, `activeCount`, `pendingCount`; errors `WorkerPoolDestroyedError`, `WorkerExitError`. `run` opts: `priority` (equal priorities run FIFO), `signal` (aborting an in-flight task rejects the caller but the task stays active until the worker replies), `transferList`. String `filename` is a cwd-relative path or URL; the worker receives `workerData.userData`; non-Error throws reject with the cloned value; a worker that fails at startup rejects queued tasks and is not respawned. Worker module must export a `default` function. Use for CPU-bound tasks that would block the event loop.

## Type Safety / Branded Types

- `@dolphin278/vjuga/TaggedUnion.js`: `TaggedUnion` — `{ tag, value }` discriminated unions with exhaustive match. `variant(tag, value)`, `match(union, handlers)`, `is(union, tag)`. `match` throws `TypeError` for a missing handler: validate untrusted input first. Use for 3+ variant sum types; for ok/err prefer `Result`.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/ISOTimestamp.js`: `ISOTimestamp` — branded string for ISO 8601 datetimes. `isoTimestamp(str)`, `fromDate`, `toDate`, `fromEpochMs`, `now` (~40% faster than `Date.toISOString`). Rejects impossible dates and hour 24; `fromEpochMs` handles negative/fractional/large ms. Use at API string boundaries; use `Date` internally for arithmetic.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/UnixTimestamp.js`: `UnixTimestamp` — branded number for Unix epoch seconds. `unixTimestamp(n)`, `fromDate`, `toDate`, `now`, `fromISO`, `toISO`. The brand does not enforce seconds or integers (a millisecond value passes). Use when your API serializes timestamps as integer seconds.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/UUID.js`: `UUID` — branded string for RFC 9562 UUIDs. `uuid(str)` validates + brands (lowercases; accepts Nil/Max, exported as `NIL`/`MAX`); `v4()` random; `v7()` timestamp-sortable; `version(id)`. Prevents passing arbitrary strings where IDs are required.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/Immutable.js`: `Immutable` — deep `readonly` type wrapper. `make(value)` is a zero-cost identity cast. Use at API boundaries where callers must not mutate returned data. Type-only; no runtime enforcement.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/Ref.js`: `Ref` — mutable reference cell `{ contents: T }`. `make(initial)`, `get(ref)`, `set(ref, value)`. Use when passing mutable primitives into closures or across module boundaries.

## Functional Utilities

- `@dolphin278/vjuga/FunctionUtils.js`: `FunctionUtils` — function types, branded-number constructors, and composition. `Fn`, `Fn1`, `Fn2`, `Predicate`, `Lazy` (all bind `this: void`). `pipe(f,g,h)` left-to-right (needs at least 1 function; typed up to 5, variadic beyond). `partial`, `partialNamed`, `tuple`, `tupled`, `spread`, `unreachable`. Branded constructors: `positiveInteger` (also a `NonNegativeInteger`), `nonNegativeInteger`, `integer`, `positiveNumber`.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/FunctionReference.js`: `FunctionReference` — serializable function pointers for cross-context dispatch. `resolve("./file.ts#exportName")` → function via dynamic `import()`. String refs are `file:` URLs or cwd-relative paths (not caller-relative); prefer `new URL("./x.js#fn", import.meta.url)`. Hash is percent-decoded. Use for cross-thread or cross-process dispatch where closures cannot be serialized.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/Memoization.js`: `Memoization` — function memoization with pluggable cache and key strategy. `memoize(fn, opts?)` caches results keyed by `JSON.stringify(args)` by default (collides for `null`/`undefined`/`NaN`, Maps/Sets, `-0`; throws on BigInt — pass `cacheKeyFn`). Unbounded by default: pass `opts.cache`, any `MemoizationCache` (`get`/`has`/`set`, e.g. a `Map` or an `LRUCache` adapter). Rejected promises are cached. `once(fn)` for lazy init; retries after a throw.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/MemoryPool.js`: `MemoryPool` — LIFO object pool for allocation-free hot paths. `make({ factory, reset?, maxSize?, minSize? })`, `acquire(pool)`, `release(pool, obj)`, `withAcquire(pool, fn)`; `make` throws `RangeError` on invalid `maxSize`/`minSize`; errors `MemoryPoolExhaustedError`, `MemoryPoolMinSizeError`. Use in hot loops creating and discarding thousands of same-shape objects per tick.

## Schema & Validation

- `@dolphin278/vjuga/schema/Schema.js`: `Schema` — data-first type schema with TypeScript type inference. 14 kinds: `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `null`, `literal`, `enum`, `object`, `array`, `tuple`, `record`, `union`, `optional`, `nullable`. Constructors for null/enum are `null_()` / `enum_()`. `S.Infer<typeof schema>` extracts TypeScript type; `toJsonSchema` / `fromJsonSchema` convert to and from JSON Schema. `object()` rejects undeclared own keys unless `{ additionalProperties: true }`; `number()` rejects NaN/±Infinity. Feeds `Validate`, `JSON`, and `TOON`.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/schema/Validate.js`: `Validate` — code-generated validators via `new Function`. `validate(schema)` compiles once at init; returns `Result<T, SchemaError>` per call. Checks own properties only; unions accept a value only if some variant fully validates it; discriminated unions dispatch in O(1). Use on hot paths (HTTP request bodies, queue payloads).
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/schema/JSON.js`: `schema/JSON` — code-generated JSON serializers and parsers. `parse(schema)` is a typed one-pass parse + validate returning `Result<T, SchemaError>`; `stringify(schema)` emits exactly the schema's keys (non-finite numbers → `null`) and is not faster than native `JSON.stringify` once the output is consumed. Strips own `__proto__` keys. Compile at init scope.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/schema/TOON.js`: `TOON` — Token-Oriented Object Notation: ~50% smaller than JSON for tabular arrays (~20% for flat objects, little for nested data). `stringify(schema)` / `parse(schema)`. Tabular array syntax, indentation-based nesting; nested list items and discriminated unions supported; unsupported shapes throw at compile time. Use for LLM context windows, config files, structured logs.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/schema/ValidationError.js`: `ValidationError` — structured `Error` subclass with `path`, `expected`, `received` fields. Use when building custom validators that return `Result<T, ValidationError>`.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/schema/Codegen.js`: `Codegen` — `new Function` compilation plumbing (CodeBuffer, ref tracking, variable naming, injection-safe literal emission: `jsLiteral`, `eqExpr`, `neExpr`). Used internally by `Validate`, `JSON`, `TOON`. Application code does not typically import this directly.

## I/O

- `@dolphin278/vjuga/HTML.js`: `HTML` — HTML entity escaping. `escape(str)` encodes `& < > " '`. 2–3x faster than regex replace when escapes are present, on par for short clean strings. Not sufficient for JSON inside `<script>` (`JSON.stringify` alone is unsafe there). Use whenever interpolating user content into HTML markup.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/HttpServer.js`: `HttpServer` — minimal HTTP/1.1 server that bypasses `node:http` overhead (no `IncomingMessage`, no `EventEmitter`, no `writeHead` serialization). Keep-alive, pipelining and backpressure. API: `make(handler, options?)`, `listen`, `close` (waits for in-flight responses), `respond`, `respondRaw`, `respondBuffer`, `precompute`, `getHeader`, method constants `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE`/`PATCH` (unknown methods → 0). Options: `maxHeaderSize` (default 64 KiB → 431), `maxBodySize` (1 MiB → 413), `headersTimeout` (60 s), `keepAliveTimeout` (5 s, idle only), `onError`. Strict framing: 400 + close on invalid/conflicting Content-Length, bare LF or folded headers; 501 on Transfer-Encoding. Handlers must answer through `respond*`. No HTTP/2 or chunked encoding. Use only when profiling shows `node:http` as the bottleneck.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/JSON.js`: `JSON` — typed JSON parsing with prototype-pollution protection. `safeParse(str)` → `Result<JSONValue, string>` (strips `__proto__`/`constructor`, including `\u`-escaped spellings). `parse(str)` → `JSONValue | undefined`. Use `safeParse` for all untrusted input.

## Property-Based Testing

- `@dolphin278/vjuga/Arbitrary.js`: `Arbitrary` — composable generators with integrated shrinking (rose trees). `integer`, `nat`, `float`, `bigint`, `date`, `string`, `boolean`, `array`, `uniqueArray`, `dictionary`, `record`, `tuple`, `oneOf`, `frequency`, `subarray`, `map`, `chain`, `filter`, `constant`, `constantFrom`, `letrec`, `gen`. Shrinking composes automatically; integer/bigint/date cover the full range at size >= 100; `Tree.shrinks` must be re-iterable.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/Property.js`: `Property` — PBT runner. `assert(arb, predicate, opts?)` runs N random cases and shrinks failures. `assertAsync` for async predicates. `check`/`checkAsync` return raw `CheckResult`. Options: `numRuns`, `seed`, `maxShrinkEvaluations`, `timeoutMs`, `path` (replay a failure: format `run@size:idx…`, same `seed`; evaluates the predicate once). Use inside `node:test`.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/StatefulTest.js`: `StatefulTest` — model-based stateful testing via command sequences. `assertStateful({ initialModel, initialReal, commands })`; also `assertStatefulAsync`, `checkStateful`, `checkStatefulAsync`. Command generators receive the live model (generation is interleaved with execution). `maxShrinkEvaluations`; `timeoutMs` bounds shrinking. Use for stateful APIs (caches, queues, state machines) where bugs arise from specific operation orderings.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/CoverageGuided.js`: `CoverageGuided` — time-boxed fuzzing. `fuzz(arb, target, opts?)` is random; `fuzzAsync` adds V8 coverage feedback (via `node:inspector`) with a capped corpus (`maxCorpus`, default 256) mutated by shrink-tree walks (simpler inputs only). `config.corpus` runs first. Use for parsers, validators, serializers. Coverage feedback is ~5–10x slower per run than PBT; not portable to browsers.
- `@dolphin278/vjuga/PRNG.js`: `PRNG` — deterministic, splittable SplitMix64 PRNG. `seed(bigint)`, `make(seed)`, `next(rng)`, `nextInt(rng, lo, hi)`, `split(rng)`. Use for reproducible random sequences with independent sub-streams. Not cryptographic.

## Key Constraints

- Zero external dependencies — no npm packages at runtime.
- ESM-only (`"type": "module"`) — extensionless subpaths are supported; `.js` subpaths remain compatible.
- Node.js >=22 required.
- All modules are standalone files — import only what you use.
- `WorkerPool` and `HttpServer` use Node.js built-ins — not available in browsers or edge runtimes.
- `CoverageGuided` uses `node:inspector` — not portable to browsers.
- No default exports — all modules use named exports.
- No root export — import `@dolphin278/vjuga/<Module>` or `@dolphin278/vjuga/schema/<Module>`.
- Module-level API style: create with `make(...)`, operate with free functions `Module.fn(handle, ...)`.
